Kernel/image cardinalities of integer matrices on Z/n follow Smith normal form: |ker A_n|=n^(t-r)Πgcd(n,d_i); quotient invariant I(n)=n^aΠ gcd(n,d_i)^epsilon with a>=0 because at large primes outside all d_i, I(p)=p^a must be a positive integer. Hence finite families of sentences depend, outside a finite n cutoff, on capped valuations at finitely many primes. Enlarge prime set and caps to encode small n distinctly; tau(n)=(capped valuation vector, indicator n>=N) is a surjective bounded morphism onto a finite directed poset, with explicit multiple-raising back lifts. Atoms are constant on fibers and modal formula values descend, proving Grz.2 lower bound from known finite-directed-poset soundness. Prime-order-element group sentences induce bounded morphisms onto every finite Boolean lattice and realize all valuations, so the published Grz.2 Boolean-lattice completeness gives the reverse inclusion. Independent 7807 explicit fixed-quotient back lifts checked on 188 signature states, corroborating but not proving infinite Baur–Monk locality.
